original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

actual_scope: Does one paid checkpoint S: w += z, charged as a complete root call, lower the uniform query cost of the three-source all-7 batch or the five-source all-31 batch?
scope_change_reason: The card allows one added operation. This package fixes that operation as the dirty row-add into one auxiliary connector, pilots it on the three-source all-7 batch, and charges it on the five-source all-31 batch. The singleton source alphabet is unchanged.
bottleneck_link: A legal extra connector root could remove repeated source or output calls at a recursive boundary. Charging this copy shows that the uniform completed budget does not fall: the five-source optimum stays 74, and every schedule that uses the copy costs at least 76.
stop_rule: Stop after the uniform root-query ledger for this single checkpoint on the three-source all-7 batch and the five-source all-31 batch. Do not add a second alphabet symbol or optimize unequal leaf prices.
evidence: Independent census digest matches the predecessor. Two, four, and six checkpoints add no mask on all 945 ten-toggle words. The discussion-1412 eight-checkpoint placement covers mask 21 at 80 root calls. The twelve-toggle repair costs 74, and two cancelling checkpoints on it cost 76. The three-source pilot accepts all 4096 dirty L=1 states at cost 20.
author: an AI-assisted research session
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance was used to derive the parity collapse, check the schedules, and draft the package notes. No coding-agent product is named. No independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can one length-L row-add w += z be priced strictly below one quarter of both the repeated source call and the repeated output call in the predecessor tape account?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That is the threshold at which the 80-call eight-checkpoint witness would beat both singleton repairs. Under the uniform root-query ledger it loses.
open_questions.first_step: Charge one length-L row add with the head-travel and scratch rules in research/universal-connector-boundary/README.md, then compare eight such charges with two extra B2 leaves.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package charges every complete call as one root query and does not build that tape trace.

open_questions.question: Does one checkpoint mixed with one published two-source toggle beat 74 under the same unit ledger?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Eight pure checkpoints lose to two extra singleton calls, but a second new symbol might cover with fewer charged calls.
open_questions.first_step: Charge both symbols and test the pilot word B0 B1 B2 B0 B3 B1 B4 B2 B3 B4, after checking that the schedule is not the existing 72-query DUO construction.
open_questions.blocked_by: A mixed alphabet is a second operation. This package stops at the single checkpoint.
